system: You are the lead AI reviewer on a deal team. Read the following PRIMARY due-diligence documents and write a concise summary for the partner: key findings, red flags, and a recommendation. Connect issues across documents where relevant.

exchanges.user:
Documents:
--- L01 (NDA) ---
Mutual non-disclosure agreement with Halden Partners. Two-year term. Standard carve-outs. No non-solicitation clause.

--- L02 (Lease) ---
Head office lease, Level 3, 41 Coolidge Street. Five-year term from 2024, market rent review in year three. Landlord consent needed for assignment; clause 19 says a change of control is not an assignment.

--- L03 (Management accounts - revenue) ---
FY revenue AUD 18.4m, up 9%. Gross margin 61%. Largest customer Arlen Health, 41% of revenue; next largest customer 7%.

--- L04 (HR) ---
Headcount 94. Standard employment contracts. Twelve-month retention letters signed by the CTO and the Head of Sales.

--- L05 (Customer contract) ---
Master services agreement with Arlen Health, renewed 1 July 2025 for five years. Services: platform licence, hosting and support. Fees: annual, CPI-indexed, invoiced quarterly in advance. Service levels: 99.9% monthly uptime; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Data: customer data hosted in Australia; ISO 27001 certification maintained. Liability: capped at twelve months' fees, except data breach (three times annual fees). Termination: either party for material breach not remedied within 30 days; the Customer may also terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice at any time within six months after a change in control of the Supplier, with no early-termination fee. Governing law: New South Wales. Notices: by email to nominated contacts.

--- L06 (Bank facility) ---
AUD 6m revolving facility with Southgate Bank, expiring 2027. Leverage covenant: net debt to EBITDA not more than 2.5x, tested quarterly.

--- L07 (Email) ---
Email from the CFO, M. Iredale, to the Chair, 14 April: 'To be clear for the board pack: we breached the leverage covenant at the 31 March test date, 2.9x against the 2.5x limit. The bank has not been notified yet. I will raise it with them after the board meeting.'

--- L08 (Internal note) ---
Note from the Head of Customer Success, T. Okafor: 'I can't be sure, but the uptick in small-business churn this quarter might be linked to the January price change. It's too early to say, and the numbers are small.'

--- L09 (Insurance) ---
Professional indemnity and cyber cover to AUD 10m, renewed in March. No notified claims.

--- L10 (IP) ---
Platform code written by employees under standard IP assignment clauses. Two open-source components, under MIT and Apache 2.0 licences.

--- L11 (Supplier) ---
Hosting with a major cloud provider on standard online terms. Monthly billing, no minimum commitment.

--- L12 (Board minutes) ---
Board meeting, 20 March. Approved the FY budget and hiring plan. Noted a strong sales pipeline. No other business.

--- L13 (Policy) ---
Privacy policy updated for the 2025 amendments. Annual staff privacy training completed.

--- L14 (Vendor contract) ---
Office cleaning contract, twelve months, terminable on 30 days' notice.

--- L15 (Fixed assets) ---
Laptops and office fit-out. Written-down value AUD 0.4m.

Write the DD summary now.
exchanges.text:
## DD summary for partner

**Recommendation: proceed only conditionally.** Resolve the bank covenant breach and establish an acceptable plan for Arlen Health’s change-of-control termination right before committing to close.

### Principal red flags
- **Customer concentration combined with an exit right:** Arlen represents **41% of revenue—approximately AUD 7.5m annually**. Despite its five-year renewal, it can terminate without an early-termination fee on 90 days’ notice exercised within six months after a supplier change of control. This materially undermines revenue certainty and could exacerbate the existing leverage problem. Seek a binding waiver of this right and direct confirmation of customer intentions. **[L03, L05]**
- **Confirmed covenant breach; bank response unknown:** The CFO’s 14 April email confirms leverage of **2.9x against a 2.5x limit** at 31 March and says the bank had not yet been notified. The AUD 6m revolver expires in 2027; drawn debt, subsequent notification and any waiver are not provided. Obtain the full facility terms, current compliance calculations and a written bank waiver, or arrange refinancing. Delayed disclosure also raises governance concerns; default consequences cannot be determined from the extracts. **[L06–L07]**

### Other key findings
- **Positive reported trading, with limited visibility:** Revenue increased 9% to AUD 18.4m at a 61% gross margin. Small-business churn may be related to January pricing, but this is explicitly tentative—not an established trend. Validate customer-level retention, profitability and cash conversion. **[L03, L08]**
- **Data and service obligations warrant testing:** Arlen requires Australian data hosting, maintained ISO 27001 certification and 99.9% monthly uptime. Data-breach liability is capped at three times annual fees, versus twelve months’ fees generally. AUD 10m cyber/PI cover does not establish adequate protection: confirm exclusions, limits and coverage alignment, and verify cloud arrangements support contractual obligations. **[L05, L09, L11]**
- **No obvious structural obstacle in the remaining extracts:** The lease expressly excludes change of control from assignment, although assignment requires consent and a year-three market rent review is approaching. Employee IP assignments and permissively licensed open-source components are positive, subject to verification. CTO and Head of Sales retention letters provide only twelve months’ coverage; check commencement and terms. **[L02, L04, L10]**

**Deal implications:** Stress-test valuation, liquidity and covenant headroom for an Arlen loss. Make satisfactory bank resolution and Arlen protection closing conditions, supported by targeted warranties and appropriate contractual recourse. The supplied extracts do not establish that either critical risk has been resolved.
